title: Mirage's Help Desk
intro: This is it, Toddy. Mirage has set up a whole fake help desk.
He'll change disguises to fool you. Collect every clue you can.
At the end you'll pin the evidence on the case board and unmask him.

notify.text: We've opened ticket #4471 for your stuck swap!

banner.text: Message request · they replied to your public post

screen.context: You posted in the Northvale community: "Swap stuck again, anyone?"

msg: Chat with a live agent here:

sys: You joined a private chat with "Agent Mira · Northvale"

msg: Hi, I'm Mira! To fix the swap I need to see your screen. Please install

replies.text: Why do you need to see my screen?

msg.text: Just read me the 6-digit code we texted you

replies.text: That code says never share it. I'll use the in-app help instead.

sys.text: Agent Mira left. "Luna (Northvale Admin)" joined the chat.

msg: Supervisor here. Your wallet is at risk!

msg.text: Move your coins to this safe wallet: 0x7Ee…a1F

replies.text: Real staff never tell you to move coins. Report.
I'll check on Northvale's official site first

tick.label: Fake tick
tick.lens: The ✔ is typed into the name. No real badge after the handle.

handle.label: Not the official handle
handle.lens: @northvale.helpdesk.live, joined last week. The official account is @northvale.
handle.why: Extra words like helpdesk or live are a favourite disguise.

dm_first.label: They messaged first
dm_first.lens: They found your public post and messaged you.
dm_first.why: Real support answers inside the app, not in surprise DMs.

chatlink.label: Private chat link
chatlink.lens: This link takes you away to a private chat they control.
chatlink.why: Moving you to a private place is how scammers cut you off from help.

screenshare.label: Screen-share app
screenshare.lens: RemoteHelp Pro would let them see and control your phone.
screenshare.why: Never install remote-access apps because a stranger asks.

otp.label: Wants your code
otp.lens: That code is the key to your account.
otp.why: Login codes are for you only. Anyone asking for one is stealing your account.

swap.label: Disguise swap
swap.lens: "Agent Mira" vanished and an "admin" appeared in the same chat.
swap.why: When the person changes but the pressure stays, it's one con artist in two costumes.

move.label: Move coins to a "safe" wallet
move.lens: That "safe wallet" belongs to whoever wrote this message.
move.why: No real company ever tells you to move your coins to a wallet they give you.

ticket.label: Ticket number
ticket.why: Ticket numbers look official, but anyone can make one up. It proves nothing alone.

actions.label: Use the help button inside the Northvale app

block_report.line: Reported. Wrenly traced every fake account back to one con artist.

verify.line: Northvale's in-app help confirmed: no Agent Mira, no Luna, no ticket #4471.

go_ahead.line: The "safe wallet" was Mirage's. The coins are gone.

what_if.go_ahead: Any request to move your coins somewhere "safe" is the final trick. Stop there and report.
what_if.verify: Checking in the official app was safe. Reporting as well gets all the fake accounts removed.

verdicts.text: One scammer pretending to be Northvale support and an admin
Real Northvale support, just being careful

board.explain: Fake tick, a look-alike handle, a private chat, a code request and a costume change. One con artist, many masks.

golden_rule: When someone "helpful" moves you to a private chat and keeps changing faces, it's one con artist in many masks.

quick_check.q: Support asks you to move your coins to a "safe wallet" right now. What do you do?

options.text: Stop, don't move anything, and report

quick_check.explain: A "safe wallet" from a stranger is their wallet.

hints.nudge: Look at where they want to take you.

rows.v: None. The ✔ is typed into the name

kit.label: Check link
kit.title: Where the chat link really goes

rows.k: Will support ask for a login code?
Will support take control of your phone?

rows.v: Answers inside the app, not in surprise DMs
